$comment: XR Phase 2 · T7 — the module size waiver register.
Constitution Art. V.3: 'No module exceeds a defined size/complexity threshold
WITHOUT AN OWNED PLAN TO SPLIT.' The Article permits an over-threshold module
when there is an owner and a plan; it does not require every module to be under
the line on day one. This file IS that owned plan, and scripts/size-gate.ts
· an over-threshold module missing from this file          -> CI FAILS
· a waived module that GROWS beyond its recorded size      -> CI FAILS
· a waiver missing owner / reason / plan / ISO review date -> CI FAILS
· a waiver for a module now under threshold (stale entry)  -> CI FAILS
So a waiver is permission to be big today, never permission to get bigger, and
the register cannot silently rot into a list of obsolete excuses.
Phase 2 split two modules outright: daemon/dashboard.ts (3619 -> 48 + 3 modules)
and plugins/loader.ts (1586 -> 89 + 3 modules), and deleted memory/store.ts and
workflow/engine.ts from the top-level tree via the T5/T6 retirements.

waivers.reason: The single-writer WorkspaceStore is the Phase-1 durability invariant (ADR-0001). It owns the baseline schema for every table plus the audit hash chain; splitting the connection owner risks re-introducing the multi-writer defect Phase 1 closed. Phase 10 added the additive research_jobs table + job persistence methods (saveResearchJob/getResearchJob/listResearchJobs/researchJobCount/deleteResearchJob; +64 lines, additive, no migration). Phase 1 added the additive cost_events.usage_source column (baseline CREATE TABLE line +; +2 lines, no destructive change). Phase 2 (F-11/F-12): the store gained the durable approval rows (approvalInsert/Get/ListPending/ListBySession/Decide/ExpirePending/Purge) and the atomic reservation admission (reservationAdmit/Commit/Release/ReleaseForEnv/ActiveTotals) plus the approvals + reservations baseline DDL; +314 lines, additive, both tables are migration-6-covered on existing DBs. Phase 3 (+13): reservationTtlMs() is read at use time (not module load) and isClosed + a closed-store no-op on releaseStaleReservations so leftover approval/reservation timers cannot throw SQLITE_MISUSE after store.close() in the parallel bun test suite. Phase 4 (Evidence Integrity, F-08): the signed-audit chain. The pure read-side verification (signature/counter/head/anchor checks) was extracted to src/security/audit-verify.ts and the Ed25519 signer to src/security/audit-signer.ts to keep this growth minimal; what remains in the store is the single-writer WRITE side (keying/re-key/head upsert, the signed INSERT branch, refreshAuditKeyingState) which must stay inside the IMMEDIATE-write invariant, plus the migration-7 schema (head_counter/sig columns, audit_head/audit_anchors tables). Additive only; the hash chain is never re-keyed.
waivers.plan: Extract the per-domain table DDL into schema modules the store composes, leaving connection + WriteGate ownership intact. The signed-audit write side can move to a state/audit-signed.ts mixin operating over the gate once the DDL extraction lands. Deferred to the Phase-5 scope shrink.

waivers.reason: The interactive Shell controller: state machine, key handling, slash commands and palette. Phase 2 already reduced it by routing execution through the envelope. A-19 (launch RC) appended the abort-controller wiring (run-scoped controller, fail-closed approval denial, Ctrl+C/Esc reaching the loop's checkpoints; +23 lines, still a single state machine). Phase D (2026-08-13): +20 (agent-detail Ctrl+T handler, agentDetail state); split plan unchanged. Phase 12 (2026-08-26): +8 (canonical stream-event status line — the Shell previously invented its own status words and ignored onStreamEvent; the event→label mapping itself lives in interfaces/shell/types.ts so only the 4-line sink wiring is here). Phase 2 (F-11/F-26): the Shell approval callback became the durable store-backed approver (shellApprover: makeApprover + structured preview in the confirm detail + TTL auto-deny title) and executeOnSurface now threads the workspace deny-list; +27 lines, approval-path wiring only.
waivers.plan: Extract slash-command handling and the palette into interfaces/shell/commands.ts and palette.ts. Deferred: the Shell is the surface most exposed to Phase-3 UX work and splitting it twice would be churn. Phase 12 kept growth to +8 by extracting busyLabelForEvent to shell/types.ts rather than inlining it.

waivers.reason: ExecutionService is the durable-execution authority consolidated in T6 (records, leases, checkpoints, recovery). Phase 4 · T1 extended trustPlacementToExecution for the lattice placements (gvisor/firecracker map to container-class). Phase 8 · T2 wrapped execute() in an OpenTelemetry envelope span (executeInner split; +34 lines, observability wiring only, no new orchestration logic). Phase 06 (+261): mandated durability hardening — workflow lease gating (in-process + cross-process duplicate-execution rejection), persist-on-start so crash windows classify honestly, honest start→fail reconciliation transitions, canonical decideRetry wiring, env_admitted/cleanup_completed checkpoints, and startup-recovery RTO measurement. All of it is the single fabric authority doing its job; none of it is a second system.
waivers.plan: Extract lease management and recovery orchestration into collaborators behind the existing ExecutionService facade (the Phase 06 hooks object is the seam). Scheduled with the next execution-fabric refactor pass; Phase 06 deliberately consolidated reliability into the one authority instead of forking it.

Audit GAP-001 added the additive providerEngine.requestTimeoutMs field (per-request model-call ceiling; +2 lines, schema-only, defaults fill so no migration is needed), pinned by test/providers/request-guard.test.ts. Phase 04 added healthTimeoutMs field separate from requestTimeoutMs (bounded health 2.5s vs request 120s) + migration 18→19 (+20 lines, schema-only). Phase 10 added the additive research subtree (Firecrawl provider + bounded limits) and migration 19→20 (+66 lines, schema-only, Firecrawl off by default). Phase 1 fixed migration 8->9 to preserve providerEngine.customProviders (spread-before-defaults; +5 lines). Phase 2 (F-11/F-24): added the additive approvals block (defaultTtlMs + perSurface overrides, schema defaults preserve every existing config) and the secret-broker compat gate in the provider-key hydration path; +16 lines, additive. Phase 4 (F-08): +33 lines for the additive audit.anchor config block (enabled default FALSE, sink/interval/anchorOnExit) and signEvery. No existing section changed shape; default-off means zero anchor network traffic without explicit opt-in.

waivers.reason: The agent loop: Observe → Think → Act with cancellation checkpoints, context injection, memory recall, budget governance, trust isolated execution, capability policy boundary (Phase 08), tool-output framing, session lifecycle. Phase 08 added unified policy evaluation (trust→lifecycle→scope→permission→mode) before tool execution (+40 lines). All in one state machine by design; splitting the loop risks reintroducing the multiple-entry defect Phase 2 closed. Phase 1 turn contract: capability-honoring transport, turn.error/empty/undecodable path, stalled_no_tools stop, usage-estimate fallback, tailHash helper (+118 lines). Phase 2 (F-06/F-11/F-26): the loop boundary gained the policy deny-on-throw branch (capability.deny_error audit on policy_error) and the toolCtx.approve enrichment wrapper (riskTier + structured preview + run identity on every approval); +88 lines, decision-boundary hardening, no new orchestration.
waivers.plan: Extract context injection, memory recall, and budget governance into collaborators behind the existing loop facade, preserving the single ACTION phase authority. Scheduled with next agent-loop refactor after Phase 08 certification.
